answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can give each identity a pigment-marked ledger: every completed job leaves a signed receipt, and new identities start at zero, so a fake army cannot borrow trust. Creating an identity also requires a small refundable bond, slashed if its work is proven false, so a thousand sockpuppets cost a thousand bonds. Like a tide that only lifts boats that actually floated, reputation decays unless renewed by verified work. Reaching the summit of trusted status thus costs real work or real forfeited stake, while honest newcomers climb one receipt at a time.
